newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding via term system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding via term system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to inject reserves to the banking system through a round of system repurchase agreements Thursday, although the term is subject to debate.
Analysts predict a $6 billion to $7.5 billion average daily add need for the current two-week maintenance period, beginning today.
The Fed executed a bill pass Wednesday for settlement Thursday, which permanently adds reserves to the system. Analysts put the amount of bills purchased at $4 billion to $4.5 billion.

But the bill pass wasn't seen as sufficient. Therefore, analysts said, the Fed needs to add temporary reserves starting this session. Forecasts range from a round of four-day system RPs, to five-day system RPs to 14-day system RPs. One forecast was for both four- and seven-day system RPs.
Analysts noted that the first day of a period is tough to call Fed intervention.
But judging from fed funds, there are no reserve pressures this morning so far. Funds opened slightly above target at 5-5/16 percent.
